competitors.description:
We need a crypto wallet built for the average SoFi customer, but still valuable to the crypto degen.

I'm thinking...
- MPC custody. No key's to lose, self custody, biometric driven.
- Holds assets, liabilities and identity. For example, KYC credentials that can be reused.
- @Figure YLDS as the fiat on/off ramp. Pays interest on your cash, 24x7 usable.
- Debit/credit card to bridge to fiat (until you can buy your coffee with YLDS). Rewards in cash, crypto and OPEN stocks?
- High yield on YLDS/fiat through democratized prime. Expand to other DeFi protocols over time.
- Robust dApp universe. Initially OPEN, democratized prime, Hastra.
- L1 interoperability. Solana, Ethereum, Provenance, etc.
- Agentic PA. "Get me a ticket from SFO to EWR on the 5th at the best price possible."

What else am I missing here?

@mattconroy @juneou @MBTannenbaum

competitors.title: You're right—each predecessor chain had its own partnerships: Fireblocks with Sologenic back in 2023
competitors.description:
You're right—each predecessor chain had its own partnerships: Fireblocks with Sologenic back in 2023, and BitGo with Coreum in early 2024.

The key difference now with TX is full execution on integration from end to end. The team has rolled out native, unified support for the combined TX ecosystem and $TX token rather than just legacy carry-overs. This means seamless custody, transactions, and institutional access built directly into the single merged platform, not siloed across old chains. It's still early (TGE is just days away), so real adoption will tell the story, but this isn't rehashing old news—it's deliberate consolidation and upgrade under one roof.  Your fair skepticism is valide, but in my opinion the updates do show active progress on unifying everything which is what the whole point of merging within $TX. Thanks!

competitors.title: I’ve been on several community calls over the past few weeks. There’s clear excitement, but also und
competitors.description:
I’ve been on several community calls over the past few weeks. There’s clear excitement, but also understandable caution. Some are asking whether the COREUM/SOLOGENIC team is simply over-promising again.

In my view, integrations like Fireblocks — along with the recent BitGo integration and exchange support announcements — materially increase credibility. These are not small retail-facing moves; they are institutional-grade infrastructure decisions.

Does this eliminate execution risk? No. No one controls macro conditions, and global events continue to affect crypto broadly.

But the evidence we’re seeing points to a structured, pre-prepared, institutional-oriented launch path for $TX — not a rushed or improvised transition.

That meaningfully lowers the probability of classic “rug” or vaporware scenarios.

Cautious optimism is rational. Dismissing tangible infrastructure progress is not.

competitors.title: When you’re building a neobank or wallet that wants to go beyond “just holding crypto,” the question
competitors.description:
When you’re building a neobank or wallet that wants to go beyond “just holding crypto,” the question becomes simple:

How do you ship institutional-grade rails, without turning security, custody, and operations into your entire company?

That’s where @BitGo fits in the stack.

BitGo is a core partner layer for teams that need:
Custody and wallet infrastructure that’s built for scale

Policy controls + approvals + auditability (the stuff serious operators can’t ignore)

A foundation that helps you move fast without compromising on trust

At Pods, we build the product rails that sit on top of this stack, helping neobanks launch yield, loans, and DeFi products through a single integration.

BitGo + Pods is the kind of partnership we like: strong custody + clean product rails = faster launches, fewer risks, better UX.

If you’re a neobank building the next generation of financial products, this is what your stack looks like in practice.

Want to see how this stack comes together? Talk to us: https://t.co/n90OGXYmvr
